To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the threshold of conductivity for ABS composites is 5 vol% of conductive carbon and 5-10vol% of aluminium flakes.
the EMI shielding effectiveness of ABS composites with conductive carbon black and aluminium flake is strongly influenced by the electrical conductivity of the composite.
the electrical and mechanical properties and processability of ABS/Al-flake composites can be improved by using a coupling agent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the processability, electrical conductivity and mechanical properties of ABS composites.
the processability, electrical properties and mechanical properties of the ABS composites, and the relationships between them.
the processability, electrical conductivity, and mechanical properties of conducting ABS composites, which are important for the development of new materials for EMI shielding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the processability of ABS is significantly improved by adding the conductive fillers (carbon black and aluminium flake) in a range of 0-30% by weight, and the EMI shielding efficiency is enhanced by increasing the conductive filler contents in the range of 10-30% by volume.
the processability, mechanical and electrical properties can be tailored to meet specific requirements by adjusting the type and content of the conductive fillers and by using coupling agents.
the EMI shielding properties of composites are determined mainly by the filler content and its distribution in the composite, the surface treatment of the filler and the matrix.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

carbon black is a more effective EMI shielding filler than aluminium flakes, and the surface modification of carbon black with silane coupling agents can significantly improve both the processability and mechanical strength of the composite.
the electrical conductivity of ABS composites can be improved significantly by the addition of conductive filler, but this improvement is at the expense of the mechanical properties.
the electrical conductivity of the composite is strongly related to the filler type and the filler loading, while the processability and mechanical strength are closely related to the filler loading.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electrical conductivity of ABS composites is a function of the filler type and its concentration in the composite, the processing conditions, and the filler surface chemistry.
the processability of the composites is strongly dependent on the filler content and the type of conductive filler used.
the electrical conductivity of composites can be improved significantly by adding a relatively small amount of conductive filler to the polymer.
